bar_predicate_clauses: prices finite: inf/-inf/nan refused via allow_inf_nan=False; pydantic's bare float ACCEPTS all three, verified on 2.10.4 (CI) and 2.12.5 (local), so this is a real tightening and not a decoration
high >= low is a THEOREM of the two ordering clauses, kept only for its message when it co-fires, explicitly NOT counted as a guard because a check that cannot fire alone is dormant
volume EXEMPT from the zero clause: a forming session legitimately reports zero traded and a naive rule would refuse live served data

zero clause, CONDITIONAL: if no price field is negative, every price field must be strictly positive. Conditional because WTI May-2020 settled negative and the exchange cleared it. Stated as positivity rather than sibling disagreement because a literal disagreement reading would ADMIT an all-zero bar. -0.0 is caught since -0.0 == 0 is true while -0.0 < 0 is false
domain clause (second derivation): a non-negative-capable asset class may not carry a price <= 0
diverged_from_twin_predicate: Two divergences, both stated with reasons. (1) NO BRAND. The twin needs one because TypeScript is structural, so an object literal satisfying the shape IS the type and only a brand forces every route through the predicate. Python classes are nominal and pydantic runs validators on __init__, so Bar(...) is already the only door; the single documented bypass, model_construct, appears nowhere in app/ or tests/ and a test keeps it that way. (2) VOLUME IS REQUIRED, not optional. The twin made v optional to keep absent and zero apart. Widening it here is 45 read sites plus the bar_store DB column plus the served JSON contract, beyond this lane; safe_bar therefore REFUSES a None volume rather than substituting 0.0, and the absent-vs-zero gap is named in the model docstring and in leave_behind.
second_derivation: bar_domain_refusal(bar, asset_class). The asset class is derived from the SYMBOL, which this process asked for and which comes from the securities/config side; the prices are derived from the VENDOR payload. Two parties: a vendor fabricating an all-zero bar cannot also change the symbol it was requested under, and the registry cannot invent a price. Weaker than the twin's security-master because the symbol is our request rather than an independent master record, but it is genuinely two upstreams and neither can satisfy both sides alone. It is FED (not starved) at app/providers/fmp.py x4, app/backtest/data.py and app/marketdata/crypto_history.py, and a test asserts some app/ caller supplies asset_class. The universal predicate _bar_refusals is internal consistency only, and says so.

refusal_log_level: WARNING, emitted from INSIDE the model validator rather than from callers. Load bearing: pydantic ValidationError subclasses ValueError and most adapters wrap construction in `except (TypeError, ValueError): continue`, so a caller-side record would be missing on exactly the paths that need it. main.py sets the root logger to WARNING, so anything lower leaves no trace in production. A test reproduces the caller-side swallow and asserts the record survives it.

handoff: runner.py carries SEVEN more POINT_VALUES.get(sym, 1.0) fabrications that no lane owns, at approximately lines 1010 (unrealized MTM accumulation feeding the daily-loss breaker), 1067 (risk-at-stop as a fraction of NAV), 1177 (R-multiple), 1433 (realized P&L), 2005 (daily-loss-limit check), 2481 and 2916 (sizing/signal context). The coordinator verified 1010 and 1067 at source and they are real: 1067 computes total += abs(price - st.stop_price) * pv * abs(qty) then returns total / nav. CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER REPORT, which was OVERSTATED: I wrote 'a /ES position's risk is understated 50x'. That is WRONG and I verified the correction at source rather than accepting it. /ES IS in POINT_VALUES at 50.0, so the default never applies to it; /ES is not even in the bot universe. The exposure is any futures symbol ABSENT from the 51-key table, not /ES. BOUND, verified at runtime: ALLOWED_SYMBOLS has 23 entries (15 futures roots, all micro/mini), ALL 23 are present in POINT_VALUES, normalize_universe keeps only ALLOWED_SYMBOLS, and the only BotPositionState write site (runner.py:2886) takes its symbol from the runner's normalized-universe iteration. So for any symbol currently in the catalog the 1.0 default is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE and the defect is LATENT. THE OPEN QUESTION, stated rather than answered by assumption: whether a PERSISTED BotPositionState row can carry a symbol that is no longer in POINT_VALUES. It is live, and more concretely than 'an external reconcile' -- at runner.py:2771-2772 the state load applies `symbol.in_(universe)` ONLY when risk_v2 is off, so under risk_v2 state rows for symbols that have left the bot's universe ARE loaded into `states`, and `states` is precisely what feeds the 1010/1067 risk computations and _reconcile_external_closes. Reaching the default therefore requires a symbol to leave ASSET_CATALOG or POINT_VALUES while a BotPositionState row for it survives. I did NOT establish whether catalog entries have ever been removed, so I do not claim the path has been taken -- only that the filter which would have bounded it is deliberately not applied on that branch. Not fixed here because each site needs a trading-policy decision about what the bot does when it cannot size a position, and another lane is active in the file. SECOND (NOW RESOLVED, not by me): _deposit_exit_outcome did float(realized or 0.0), which would have converted the absence _own_realized now returns into a fabricated 0.0 R-multiple. I left it untouched per the dispatch because another lane was editing that function. That lane's PR #361 merged into main mid-flight and replaced it with r_multiple_or_decline(realized, ...) which branches on `is None` explicitly (their comment: '`is None`, never `or`: realized == 0.0 is a REAL observation'). Verified by reading the merged file, not assumed: the two changes COMPOSE -- my absence now becomes an RUnmeasurable decline carrying its own basis instead of a break-even verdict on a trade whose result was never observed. Refusing to reach into the other lane's function was the right call and cost nothing. THIRD: the frontend deriveVolRegime and atmIvForExpiry apply `?? 0` to surface cells, re-fabricating the zero downstream of the API fix; behaviour-preserving and left alone because deciding what a chart shows for an unsolved cell is a UI decision.
